title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #10

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On a physical map, what colour is often used for high mountains? (1 mark)
   A. White
   B. Pink
   C. Blue
   D. Brown

2. Which valley runs from north to south through Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Great Rift Valley
   B. The Coast Valley
   C. The Tana Valley
   D. The Kisumu Valley

3. Why does Kenya not have summer and winter like countries far from the equator? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya has no rain
   B. Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   C. Kenya is too small
   D. Kenya has no sun

4. Which season usually follows the long rains in Kenya's common pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Long rains again
   B. Cool or cold season
   C. Hot season
   D. Short rains

5. Why is it dangerous to cross a flooded road? (1 mark)
   A. The road is shorter
   B. There is no traffic
   C. Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   D. Water is always clean

6. What is the name of the organisation that looks after most museums in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya Power
   B. National Museums of Kenya
   C. Kenya Airways
   D. Kenya Ports

7. What might happen if all drivers stopped working? (1 mark)
   A. More crops would grow
   B. Schools would close forever
   C. Nothing would change
   D. Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals

8. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give? (1 mark)
   A. Learning
   B. Health care
   C. Transport
   D. Food

9. How do religious leaders help the community? (1 mark)
   A. They drive buses
   B. They teach values and comfort people
   C. They sell food
   D. They repair roads

10. What is trade? (1 mark)
   A. Buying and selling goods
   B. Growing crops only
   C. Building houses
   D. Playing games

11. Which is a way of showing appreciation for others? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at their work
   B. Saying thank you
   C. Breaking their tools
   D. Ignoring their help

12. Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots? (1 mark)
   A. Write the county name only
   B. Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   C. Draw a river
   D. Colour the whole map blue

13. What do we call an area where many people live close together? (1 mark)
   A. Empty
   B. Densely populated
   C. Wild
   D. Sparsely populated

14. Which of these counties has a very dense city population? (1 mark)
   A. Wajir
   B. Nairobi
   C. Marsabit
   D. Turkana

15. Which is a traditional food eaten in many parts of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Pizza
   B. Sushi
   C. Ugali
   D. Hamburger

16. Which of these is an aspect of traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. Rivers
   B. Mountains
   C. Rainfall
   D. Traditional food

17. Which artefacts are carved at Kisii and sold to visitors? (1 mark)
   A. Glass windows
   B. Soapstone carvings
   C. Iron bridges
   D. Plastic toys

18. When giving peer feedback, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Say something you like and something to improve, politely
   B. Say only bad things
   C. Say nothing
   D. Laugh

19. What is a motto? (1 mark)
   A. A school bag
   B. A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   C. A class register
   D. A school bell

20. Which of these is a school value? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating
   B. Stealing
   C. Bullying
   D. Honesty

21. Where is titanium mined in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kwale
   B. Kisumu
   C. Nyeri
   D. Nakuru

22. What is an economic activity? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A game after school
   C. Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   D. A holiday

23. How do industries help farmers? (1 mark)
   A. They teach only
   B. They cut farms
   C. They stop rain
   D. They buy the farmers' produce

24. What is one problem that industries can cause? (1 mark)
   A. Pollution
   B. More rain
   C. Less trade
   D. Fewer jobs

25. What does the project manager do? (1 mark)
   A. Prints books
   B. Drives the bus
   C. Cooks lunch
   D. Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time

26. Which of these can be a school enterprise project? (1 mark)
   A. A vegetable garden
   B. A robbery
   C. Bullying
   D. A war

27. What is a good thing to do at the end of a project? (1 mark)
   A. Forget about it
   B. Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   C. Throw away records
   D. Blame others

28. Which colour is best for a road safety bib? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Grey
   C. Bright orange or yellow
   D. Dark brown

29. Who can be a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an elder
   B. Only a rich person
   C. Only a president
   D. Nobody

30. When talking about a conflict, which kind of sentence is best? (1 mark)
   A. I will hit you
   B. You are stupid
   C. I felt hurt when...
   D. Everyone hates you

31. What does listening do for peace? (1 mark)
   A. It wastes time
   B. It helps people to understand each other
   C. It makes people angry
   D. It starts fights

32. Which of these is a correct body safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Say nothing
   B. No one should touch your private parts
   C. Keep it a secret if someone does
   D. Anyone can touch them

33. What is a responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. A toy
   B. A gift
   C. A duty you should do
   D. A secret

34. What is a ballot paper? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of book
   B. A menu
   C. A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   D. A ticket for a bus

35. What should you do if your candidate loses? (1 mark)
   A. Spread rumours
   B. Accept the results peacefully
   C. Fight
   D. Refuse to work with the winner

36. Which minister would deal with dirty toilets? (1 mark)
   A. Health and sanitation
   B. Library
   C. Music
   D. Sports

37. What is a Children's Government in school? (1 mark)
   A. The government of Kenya
   B. A group of parents
   C. A group of teachers
   D. A group of elected pupils who help to run the school

38. Where does a county government get money? (1 mark)
   A. From the national government and local fees and taxes
   B. Only from fines
   C. From nowhere
   D. Only from gifts

39. Which of these is a county government service? (1 mark)
   A. Defending the country
   B. Running county health centres
   C. Issuing passports
   D. Running the army

40. What is devolution? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of tax
   B. Ending the government
   C. Keeping all power in one place
   D. Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe the steps in a fair class election. (4 marks)

42. Explain what would happen in a community if farmers stopped growing food. (4 marks)

43. Name two duties of a pupil in school. (2 marks)

44. List four ways of caring for rivers and lakes. (4 marks)

45. Give two reasons why we obey school rules. (2 marks)

46. Explain why it is important to have a Children's Government in school. (4 marks)

47. Where can a child go for help if they are being harmed? (2 marks)

48. List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place. (4 marks)

49. The sugar factory employs 700 workers and the tea factory employs 400 workers. How many workers are there in the two factories together? Show your working. (3 marks)

50. Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely. (4 marks)

51. Explain how tourism can benefit a county and its people. (5 marks)

52. Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular. (4 marks)

53. Explain what a Children's Government is. (2 marks)

54. A bar graph shows sub-county A has 40 thousand people and sub-county B has 25 thousand. Find the total population of the two sub-counties. (3 marks)

55. Explain four ways in which rainy weather makes roads dangerous. (4 marks)

56. Describe what you should do if you are being bullied. (3 marks)

57. Explain why traditional culture is important. (3 marks)

58. Describe three ways in which pupils can take part in conserving a historic place near their school. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Brown
   Brown shows high land such as mountains.

2. A — The Great Rift Valley
   The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.

3. B — Kenya lies on the equator so temperatures change little
   Near the equator the temperature stays fairly steady, so rain and altitude decide our seasons.

4. B — Cool or cold season
   In the usual pattern, June to August is cool or cold in many places.

5. C — Water may be deep and fast and can hide holes
   Floods can carry people and vehicles away.

6. B — National Museums of Kenya
   The National Museums of Kenya manages many museums.

7. D — Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   Transport connects producers, shops and hospitals.

8. D — Food
   Farmers give food to the community.

9. B — They teach values and comfort people
   Religious leaders teach good values and care for people.

10. A — Buying and selling goods
   Trade is buying and selling.

11. B — Saying thank you
   Thanking people shows we value them.

12. B — Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
   A dot map needs a clear key.

13. B — Densely populated
   Dense means crowded.

14. B — Nairobi
   Nairobi has a large city population.

15. C — Ugali
   Ugali is widely eaten in Kenya.

16. D — Traditional food
   Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, games and ceremonies are aspects of culture.

17. B — Soapstone carvings
   Kisii is known for soapstone carving.

18. A — Say something you like and something to improve, politely
   Kind, helpful feedback improves work.

19. B — A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   A motto is a short saying of aims.

20. D — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive value.

21. A — Kwale
   Titanium is mined in Kwale County.

22. C — Work done to earn income or make goods and services
   Economic activities bring in income.

23. D — They buy the farmers' produce
   Factories need farm produce as raw materials.

24. A — Pollution
   Waste from factories can pollute air and water.

25. D — Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   The manager coordinates the work.

26. A — A vegetable garden
   A garden can be run safely by pupils.

27. B — Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   Evaluation helps us do better next time.

28. C — Bright orange or yellow
   Bright colours are easy to see.

29. A — A teacher or an elder
   Ordinary people can be good role models.

30. C — I felt hurt when...
   'I' sentences share feelings without blaming.

31. B — It helps people to understand each other
   Listening helps solve conflicts.

32. B — No one should touch your private parts
   Your body belongs to you.

33. C — A duty you should do
   Rights come with responsibilities.

34. C — A paper on which a voter marks a choice
   Voters mark ballot papers.

35. B — Accept the results peacefully
   Accepting results is part of democracy.

36. A — Health and sanitation
   Health and sanitation looks after cleanliness.

37. D — A group of elected pupils who help to run the school
   It is made up of pupils chosen by their classmates.

38. A — From the national government and local fees and taxes
   Counties get shared money and collect local fees.

39. B — Running county health centres
   Health centres are a county responsibility.

40. D — Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
   Devolution moves some power to counties.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Announce, nominate candidates, campaign, vote, count votes in public, and declare the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group of two correct steps.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: There would be a shortage of food. Traders would have nothing to sell. Prices would go up. People could become hungry and ill.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each consequence.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Follow the school rules and respect others. Accept care for property or do class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not throw rubbish into them, plant trees on the banks, do not wash or farm too close to the water, and tell adults about pollution.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Rules keep everyone safe and they help everyone to learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: It gives pupils a voice, teaches leadership, helps teachers with order and cleanliness, and teaches democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: To a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher, or to the child helpline 116.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct source of help.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,100 workers.
   Working / marking points: 700 + 400 = 1,100. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for correct sum, 1 mark for the unit.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay park and hotel fees. Guides and drivers get jobs. Hotels and shops earn money. Local crafts are sold. The county earns taxes to build roads and clinics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a group of pupils elected by their classmates to help run the school and speak for pupils, guided by a teacher.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for elected pupils, 1 mark for helping and speaking for pupils.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 65 thousand, which is 65,000 people.
   Working / marking points: 40 + 25 = 65 thousand. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 65 thousand, 1 mark for 65,000.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roads become slippery, it is harder to see, floods can sweep away people and vehicles, and water can hide holes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stay calm and do not fight back, walk away to a safe place, and tell a trusted adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives identity, teaches values, and brings people together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweep and pick up litter, report damage to an adult, and tell others why the place is important.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.
